reference.reason: The RSI-PCA prediction pane is an in-house model (rsi_pca.rs header: 'The neurotrader RSI-PCA idea, in-house'). Its only published form is the model's own repo, not a chart with a standard drawing, so there is no external look to match -- the target is our own pane: one prediction line, a zero line, a dot per signal.

draw.today: 7 'rsi pca' labels (x 586.7-796.7, y 61.4-407.1) on the price frame while the prediction pane -- one auto-scaled line, zero line, signal dots -- is drawn below. A prediction is not a price, and a word at price is not a prediction.
draw.canonical: one auto-scaled prediction line in its own pane with a zero line and a dot at each signal bar; the shape is ours, so the standard is the pane the model already has, not an external chart.

fires.our_rule: the walk-forward RSI-PCA prediction is defined on every bar after the model can fit; a label is emitted when the 95% band excludes zero (rsi_pca.rs:262-320)
fires.their_rule: there is no external drawing of this model, so no external rule to compare against; its own pane marks the crossings

rule_as_data.rule: pred = RSI-PCA walk-forward prediction (refit every 24 bars on 200) => signal when the 95% band excludes zero

warmup.before: the model refuses before 48 + 200 = 248 bars (rsi_pca.rs:237-241); the first prediction is bar 249 in a 501-bar window

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Relative Strength Index (RSI)
reference.quote: It is plotted in a separate pane below the price chart, oscillating between 0 and 100 with overbought at 70 and oversold at 30.

draw.today: 9 'rsi' labels (x 436.6-768.9, y 45.7-297.3) at price while the RSI pane -- one line, fixed 0-100, 70/30 levels -- is drawn below. The zone cross the label announces is already visible as the line passing 30 or 70.
draw.canonical: one RSI line in its own pane, fixed 0-100, levels at 70 and 30 -- the reference says it 'is plotted in a separate pane below the price chart, oscillating between 0 and 100'.

fires.our_rule: RSI(14) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses the 30 or 70 band (indicator_signals.rs:121-123, n > 15)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots RSI continuously against 30/70 and marks no zone entry; the line crossing the band is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: rsi = RSI(close, 14) => signal when rsi crosses 30 or 70

warmup.before: RSI(14) exists from bar 14; the detector requires n > 15

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, RSI Divergence indicator
reference.quote: The divergence indicator helps traders assess changes in the price trend and indicates when price will move with or against the direction of another indicator.

draw.today: 4 'rsi divergence' labels (x 511.6-807.5, y 37.9-460.3) at price while the RSI pane plus its divergence segments and dots is drawn below. The word duplicates the pane's own marks, at the wrong scale.
draw.canonical: the RSI pane with a segment joining the two RSI pivots and a dot at the confirming bar -- 'the divergence indicator ... indicates when price will move with or against the direction of another indicator'.

fires.our_rule: RSI(14) is defined on every bar; price/RSI divergences are emitted when the tail confirms them (indicator_signals.rs:160, n > 40)
fires.their_rule: TradingView's divergence tool draws the pivot-to-pivot line on the oscillator; it does not stamp a word at price

rule_as_data.rule: divergence = price makes higher high while RSI(14) makes lower high (or the bearish mirror) => segment from prior pivot to confirming pivot, dot at confirmation

warmup.before: RSI(14) exists from bar 14; the divergence detector requires n > 40

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Relative Strength Index (RSI)
reference.quote: It is plotted in a separate pane below the price chart, oscillating between 0 and 100 with overbought at 70 and oversold at 30.

draw.today: 8 'rsi family' labels (x 438.7-792.5, y 29.7-460.3) at price while the 23-line ribbon is drawn in its own fixed 0-100 pane. The ribbon is the indicator; the labels are a second draw of its name on the price axis.
draw.canonical: 23 RSI periods on one fixed 0-100 pane with 70/30 levels and a fast-to-slow gradient -- our composition of the reference's single RSI pane, which establishes the scale, the levels and the pane.

fires.our_rule: RSI(2)..RSI(24) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when all 23 sit on the same side of 50 (indicator_signals.rs:146, n > 26)
fires.their_rule: TradingView draws one RSI period continuously and has no 23-period ribbon or consensus event; the pane convention is borrowed, the signal is ours

rule_as_data.rule: for p in 2..=24: rsi[p] = RSI(close, p) => signal when all rsi[p] > 50 or all rsi[p] < 50

warmup.before: RSI(24) exists from bar 24; the detector requires n > 26

reference.quote: Overbought levels are at 80 and oversold levels are at 20.

draw.today: 50 'stochastic' labels (x 876.1-1081.9, y 324.4-486.1) at price while %K/%D with 80/20 are drawn in their own pane. The labels sit in the last fifth of the window, all saying the same word at price.
draw.canonical: %K and %D in their own pane, fixed 0-100, levels at 80 and 20 -- the reference puts overbought at 80 and oversold at 20 and marks no zone entry at price.

fires.our_rule: %K(14,3) and %D(3) are defined on every bar; a label is emitted on 80/20 zone entry and on %K crossing %D (indicator_signals.rs:225-232, n > 18)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots both lines continuously against 80/20 and marks no cross; the lines are the reading

rule_as_data.rule: %k = Stochastic(14, 3); %d = SMA(%k, 3) => signal when %k enters 80/20 or %k crosses %d

warmup.before: %K/%D exist from bar 16; the detector requires n > 18

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Commodity Channel Index (CCI)
reference.quote: Values above +100 indicate overbought conditions, while values below -100 signal oversold markets.

draw.today: 46 'cci' labels (x 65.7-1081.9, y 71.2-455.3) at price while the CCI pane with its +/-100 levels is drawn below. The oscillator is drawn correctly; the labels are its name repeated at price.
draw.canonical: one CCI line in its own pane with levels at +100 and -100 -- the reference reads 'values above +100 ... below -100' and draws no word at the bar.

fires.our_rule: CCI(20) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses +/-100 (indicator_signals.rs:242-244, n > 22)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots CCI continuously against +/-100 and marks no zone entry; the line crossing the level is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: cci = CCI(typical, 20) => signal when cci crosses +100 or -100

warmup.before: CCI(20) exists from bar 20; the detector requires n > 22

reference.quote: Williams %R (%R) is a momentum-based oscillator used in technical analysis, primarily to identify overbought and oversold conditions.

draw.today: 50 'williams r' labels (x 215.8-1081.9, y 48.2-477.3) at price while the %R pane is drawn below. The word, not the oscillator, is what the concept path adds.
draw.canonical: one %R line in its own pane, fixed -100..0, levels at -20 and -80 -- a bounded oscillator, and the reference marks no zone entry at price.

fires.our_rule: Williams %R(14) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses -80 or -20 (indicator_signals.rs:254-256, n > 16)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots %R continuously against -20/-80 and marks no cross; the line is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: wr = Williams%R(14) => signal when wr crosses -80 or -20

warmup.before: %R(14) exists from bar 14; the detector requires n > 16

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, Rate of Change (ROC)
reference.quote: The Rate of Change indicator (ROC) is a momentum oscillator. It calculates the percent change in price between periods.

draw.today: 50 'roc' labels (x 142.9-1058.3, y 60.1-447.1) at price while the ROC pane with its zero line is drawn below. The percent-change line is the indicator; the labels are its name at price.
draw.canonical: one ROC line in its own pane, auto-scaled, zero line -- 'a momentum oscillator ... the percent change in price between periods', with no mark printed at price.

fires.our_rule: ROC(12) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses zero (indicator_signals.rs:266-268, n > 14)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots ROC continuously across zero and marks no cross; the line crossing zero is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: roc = 100 * (close / close[12] - 1) => signal when roc crosses zero

warmup.before: ROC(12) exists from bar 12; the detector requires n > 14

reference.source: TradingView Help Center, True Strength Index
reference.quote: The True Strength Index indicator is a momentum oscillator designed to detect, confirm or visualize the strength of a trend.

draw.today: 39 'tsi' labels (x 100-1060.4, y 55.3-447.3) at price while the TSI pane with its signal line is drawn below. Two continuous lines become a word at price on the concept path.
draw.canonical: TSI and its signal as two lines in their own pane, zero line -- 'a momentum oscillator designed to detect, confirm or visualize the strength of a trend' -- no mark at price.

fires.our_rule: TSI(13,25,7) and its signal are defined on every bar; a label is emitted when the line crosses the signal (indicator_signals.rs:390-392, n > 40)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots both TSI lines continuously and marks no cross; the signal-line cross is a pane reading

rule_as_data.rule: tsi = TSI(close, 13, 25); signal = EMA(tsi, 7) => signal when tsi crosses signal

warmup.before: TSI(25) exists from bar 25; the detector requires n > 40

reference.quote: The Awesome Oscillator is an indicator used to measure market momentum.

draw.today: 24 'awesome' labels (x 97.9-1034.7, y 94.4-419.5) at price while the zero-anchored AO histogram is drawn below. A histogram and a word at price are two different drawings of one momentum measure.
draw.canonical: zero-anchored histogram bars in their own pane, green above zero and red below -- 'an indicator used to measure market momentum' -- with no word at price.

fires.our_rule: AO(5,34) is defined on every bar; a label is emitted when it crosses zero (indicator_signals.rs:402-404, n > 36)
fires.their_rule: TradingView plots the AO histogram continuously and marks no zero cross; the bar colour is the reading

rule_as_data.rule: ao = SMA(median, 5) - SMA(median, 34) => signal when ao crosses zero

warmup.before: AO(34) exists from bar 34; the detector requires n > 36
